newsitem.title: UK: Wlm Cook, backers dismiss "smear campaign".
newsitem.headline: Wlm Cook, backers dismiss "smear campaign".

text.p: The management and venture capital backers of steel castings specialist William Cook Plc on Friday dismissed as "distasteful" newspaper coverage of allegations of mismanagement contained in anonymous letters sent to the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI).

Several newspapers quoted from a copy of one letter addressed to the DTI asking it to look into any discrepancies among trading forecasts Cook made in 1996 prior to a hostile bid being launched by engineering group Triplex Lloyd Plc.
Triplex's latest offer, worth about 383 pence a share, was trumped by a venture-backed mbo team offering 425p last week.
A source close to William Cook told Reuters that there was no base to the allegations on forecasts, adding "it plainly is not affecting our defence against the Triplex bid".
He said the company was troubled by what appeared to be a "smear" campaign directed against current executive chairman Andrew Cook who is known for his autocratic leadership style.

These comments were echoed by a source at Electra Fleming, the venture capital house backing the mbo's 80 million stg counter-offer. This source also said the letter, and another one reported in The Guardian newspaper as making allegations about Cook's salary and expenses, was part of a concerted smear.

"Of course we recognise that Andrew Cook does not have a classic record on corporate governance. As you know, we have addressed this for the future," an Electra spokesman said, his latter point referring to a plan to make Cook chief executive, supervised by a new chairman, should the buyout plan succeed.

"We regard the type of story in today's newspaper as scurrilous and clearly part of a smear campaign. We are entirely aware of this letter (reported in the Guardian) which we suspect was written by a disgruntled ex-employee.
"We have, of course, investigated it and do not give these allegations any credence," Electra Fleming added.
"The whole thing smacks of sour grapes and an attempt to drive a wedge between management and its financial backers," Electra went on.

Market sources said that an obvious impact of the letters, which newspapers said had been circulating in London's City financial community for some time, was to highlight the gulf between Triplex's last bid and the mbo's higher cash offer.

However, a Triplex spokesman declined to comment on any implications of today's press reports, saying only that the group would stick to its guns. "Triplex has made a good offer and the City will judge it on its merits," he said.
The market, meanwhile, is suggesting that the mbo offer will easily win the day unless Triplex does in fact raise its bid.
William Cook's shares climbed to the mbo bid price of 425 pence after its launch a week ago, and have steadied there.
But Triplex shares have been under pressure since it launched its last bid and have drifted from about 210 pence two weeks ago to 187-1/2 pence today.
"Triplex Lloyd is obviously having difficulty getting backing for an increased bid," one market source said.
"Electra Fleming put their money where their mouth is, and the main argument here is about cash," he added.
